name: MeasurementProtocol
summary: Makes the method behind a measurement an object stating what it takes and what it yields, so that a figure can be recomputed and explained rather than only stored.

roles.name: MeasurementProtocol
roles.summary: The protocol as a type object: it names the phenomenon type it results in, and in order the phenomenon types it takes as inputs. What it adds to a protocol is that it says enough for a measurement to be produced, and not only enough for two figures obtained differently to be kept apart.

roles.name: SourceMeasurementProtocol
roles.summary: A protocol whose result is observed rather than computed — someone read an instrument. It takes no inputs, and it is where the numbers every calculation stands on enter the model.

roles.name: CalculatedMeasurementProtocol
roles.summary: A protocol whose result is computed from measurements of its input types by a formula it holds. Every measurement made under it is a calculated measurement and every calculated measurement is made under one, which is the constraint stated in both directions.

roles.name: Method
roles.summary: The formula a calculated protocol holds, as an object rather than as code inside the protocol, so that one piece of arithmetic can serve several protocols and a new protocol can be configured instead of written.

roles.name: CausalCalculation
roles.summary: A method deriving its result from inputs of different phenomenon types — a cost per unit from a cost and a count. Its inputs are heterogeneous, which is exactly what distinguishes it from a comparison.

roles.name: ComparativeCalculation
roles.summary: A method taking exactly two inputs of the same phenomenon type, so that its result is a comparison: this month against last, actual against planned. The cardinality and the sameness of the two types are the assertion.

roles.name: DimensionCombination
roles.summary: A method summing a measurement over the children of one dimension element, so that a figure for a country is derived from the figures for its cities. Its single input type is its result type, which is what lets it compose up a hierarchy without a case per level.

roles.name: CalculatedMeasurement
roles.summary: The measurement produced under a calculated protocol. It is an ordinary measurement to anything that reads it, which is what keeps a derived figure comparable with an observed one.

roles.name: Sources
roles.summary: The measurements a calculated measurement was computed from, kept rather than discarded once the arithmetic is done. Keeping them is what makes a figure re-explainable instead of a number whose provenance is lost.
